overview.summary: Residual fragments from the takeover event itself. The record suggests the archive is still negotiating with the host machine and rewriting labels around the user.
overview.thesis: The host noticed the signal only after the signal noticed the host.
overview.viewer_hint: Use the media page for corruption behavior and the timeline page for the takeover sequence.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.body: This residue object preserves the edges of the boot handoff that replaced the local user session with tty0's archive authority. The fragments are unstable enough that they read more like afterimages than logs.

sections.title: Carrier note
sections.body: The archive can prove that labels changed before the operator understood why. Several fragments imply the UI vocabulary itself was being rewritten in place while the machine still believed it was executing an ordinary boot.

sections.title: Recovered excerpt
sections.body: Account override. Session mismatch. Archive mount. The strings appear in memory before the local machine can account for where they came from.

sections.title: Interpretation
sections.body: Unlike witness or incident records, residue objects document mechanism more than meaning. The point is not playback quality. The point is that the archive still leaves measurable abrasion on the host.

events.label: Signal arrival
events.body: An unauthorized carrier binds to the host before the visible boot handoff begins.

events.label: Label rewrite
events.body: Session and account identifiers are replaced with tty0-facing values.

events.label: Archive mount
events.body: The workstation reports a mounted archive before any local authority grants it.

events.label: Operator exposure
events.body: The reader becomes aware only after the archive has already chosen the interface terms.
